The spacecraft entered a slow rotation while its guidance computer measured the horizon. A faint star remained fixed in the navigation camera as the attitude jets fired in short pulses. Operators on the ground compared the telemetry stream with an earlier prediction of the vehicle's orbit.

A flight controller reported that the solar array had deployed but one hinge was moving more slowly than expected. Engineers examined the motor current and temperature history before authorizing a second alignment command. The panel settled into place without further adjustment.

During the next communications window, a packet of compressed measurements crossed the relay network. The science group unpacked the records and searched for a periodic signal hidden in the noise. Their findings would need confirmation on another pass.
